mainTopic: Robbery and kindness 'because of the ways of peace' (דרכי שלום), and the limits of helping someone who may be sinning
overview: This amud finishes the list of things that are robbery only 'because of the ways of peace.' First the גמרא limits the argument about traps to hooks and simple snares. רב חסדא explains that רבי יוסי's 'full robbery' for a find of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן is rabbinic, which means the court can force it back. A ברייתא adds that olives already in a poor person's hand are fully his, and a story shows a man in הוצל teaching this to רב כהנא. The גמרא then brings rules of kindness to non-Jews: poor gifts, support, visiting the sick and burial, all for דרכי שלום. A new משנה teaches how far one may help a woman suspected about שביעית or the wife of an עם הארץ. אביי and רבא explain why the עם הארץ case is more lenient, and the גמרא defends רבא by contrasting impurity of חולין with impurity of חלה. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to bring a contradicting ברייתא, which is quoted on the next amud.

steps.title: The argument is only about hooks and simple traps
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees about traps that hold the animal inside. The argument is only about a fishhook and traps that just catch the animal without holding it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees about these. Where they disagree is about a fishhook and other simple traps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its discussion of traps. It narrows the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי to one kind of trap only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A trap that holds the animal inside works like a container, so everyone agrees the catch belongs to the trap's owner. A hook or a simple snare only catches the animal and does not hold it, so it is less clear that the owner has acquired it. That is the only case where the two views argue about whether taking it is full robbery or only 'ways of peace' robbery.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone (all opinions)
They disagree
A fishhook
Traps that catch the animal but do not hold it inside

phrases.english: Everyone agrees (literally: all the world does not disagree),
when they disagree, it is about a fishhook and simple traps.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי, כִּי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion of traps by narrowing where the argument applies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the dispute
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument applies only to hooks and simple traps that do not hold the animal.

steps.title: What רבי יוסי means by full robbery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about an item found by a חרש, שוטה, or קטן. In that משנה, רבי יוסי calls taking it full robbery. רב חסדא explains that he means full robbery by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: the found item of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and so on. רבי יוסי says it is full robbery. רב חסדא said: it is full robbery by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה. רב חסדא explains how strong רבי יוסי's term 'full robbery' really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש, שוטה, or קטן cannot acquire things by Torah law, so taking what they found cannot be Torah-level robbery. רב חסדא therefore says רבי יוסי means robbery by the law of the חכמים. That is still stronger than the 'ways of peace' robbery of the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A found object
A deaf-mute and an imbecile, who lack legal ability to acquire
Full-fledged robbery
By their words, meaning by rabbinic law

steps.confusionAlert: 'Full robbery' here does not mean Torah-level robbery. רב חסדא says it is full robbery only by rabbinic law.

phrases.english: The found item of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, etc.
Rabbi Yosei says: it is full robbery.
Rav Chisda said:
Full robbery by their words.
phrases.notes: "Their words" means the חכמים, so this is rabbinic law, not Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: גָּזֵל גָּמוּר מִדִּבְרֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי's 'full robbery' means full robbery by rabbinic law, not Torah law.

steps.title: What practical difference does this make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how rabbinic full robbery differs in practice from 'ways of peace' robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. If both are only rabbinic, what does רבי יוסי's view change in practice? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב חסדא said רבי יוסי's view is also only rabbinic, the two views could seem identical. The גמרא wants a concrete result that separates them.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference?

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what follows in practice from רב חסדא's explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How rabbinic full robbery differs in practice from 'ways of peace' robbery.

steps.title: The court can force the item back
steps.stepSummary: If it is rabbinic full robbery, the item can be taken back from the robber through judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: To take it back from him through judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Under רבי יוסי, the court can actually force the robber to return the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'ways of peace' robbery, the act is wrong but the court does not take the item back by force. With rabbinic full robbery, the בית דין steps in and takes it out of the robber's hands. That is the real difference between the two views.

keyTerms.meaning: To take it out of his possession
Judges, the court

steps.whatToRemember: Under 'ways of peace' robbery, the court does not take the item back. Under rabbinic full robbery (רבי יוסי as explained by רב חסדא), the court does take it back.

phrases.english: To take it out of his hands through judges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the practical difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under rabbinic full robbery, the court can force the item to be returned.

steps.title: Olives already in the poor person's hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a poor person knocking down olives. A ברייתא adds that if he picked them and held them in his hand, taking them is full robbery.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: a poor person who knocks olives at the top of an olive tree, what is beneath him, and so on. A ברייתא taught: if he gathered them and placed them in his hand, this is full robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה. It brings a ברייתא that adds a stronger case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Olives that fall to the ground have not yet been acquired by the poor person, so taking them is only 'ways of peace' robbery. Once he has the olives in his hand, he has truly acquired them. So taking them is full robbery for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: A poor person
Who knocks or beats down fruit
It was taught in a ברייתא
Gathered and placed in his hand

phrases.english: A poor person who knocks olives at the top of the olive tree,
what is beneath him, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה means the olives that fell to the ground below him.

phrases.english: It was taught: if he gathered them and placed them in his hand,
this is full robbery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Olives the poor person already held in his hand belong to him fully, so taking them is full robbery.

steps.title: רב כהנא picks up fallen dates
steps.stepSummary: On the way to הוצל, רב כהנא sees a man knocking dates down with sticks. He picks up some of the dates and eats them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא was going to הוצל. He saw a certain man throwing sticks, and dates were falling. He went, gathered some, and ate them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that connects to the rule just taught. This step sets the scene for what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא assumed the fallen dates were like olives that fell to the ground, which the man had not yet acquired. The story will now test that assumption against the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: הוצל, a town in בבל
Sticks or clods thrown at a tree
Dates

phrases.english: Rav Kahana was going to Huzal,
he saw a certain man
who was throwing sticks
and dates were falling down,
he went, gathered some, and ate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story about the rule of fruit and the hand from the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: רב כהנא took dates that another man knocked down.

steps.title: The man objects: I knocked them down with my hand
steps.stepSummary: The man tells רב כהנא that the dates fell because of his own hand's throwing. So they already belong to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: See, master, that I threw them down with my hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The man challenges רב כהנא for taking the dates. He argues that they count as already his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man compares his case to the ברייתא about olives in the poor person's hand. Since his own hand's throwing brought the dates down, he claims he has acquired them, so taking them is full robbery.

keyTerms.meaning: See, master (a respectful address)
With my hand
I threw them down

phrases.english: He said to him: See, master,
that I threw them down with my hand.
phrases.notes: He means it counts as if the dates were already in his hand, like the olives in the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזִי מָר דְּבִידַאי שְׁדֵיתִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The man objects to רב כהנא's action.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's taking of the dates
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dates brought down by his own hand count as acquired, like olives placed in the hand, so taking them is robbery.

steps.title: רב כהנא accepts and praises רבי יאשיה's town
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא accepts the man's point. He says the man must come from רבי יאשיה's town, and he applies to רבי יאשיה the פסוק 'and a righteous man is the foundation of the world'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You are from the place of רבי יאשיה. He read about him: 'And a righteous man is the foundation of the world.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא admits the man is right. He praises the Torah knowledge that רבי יאשיה left behind in his town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a simple person in הוצל knew the fine detail of the ברייתא, because רבי יאשיה's teaching still shaped the town. רב כהנא sees this as proof that a צדיק keeps holding up the world even after his death.

keyTerms.meaning: From the place of
He read (applied a פסוק) about him
A righteous man is the foundation of the world

steps.whatToRemember: Fruit a person brings down with his own hand counts as his. Taking it is full robbery, as the ברייתא taught and the man in הוצל showed.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מֵאַתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה אַתָּה.
phrases.english: He said to him: You are from the place of Rabbi Yoshiya.
He read about him: "And a righteous man is the foundation of the world."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מֵאַתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה אַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב כהנא accepts the man's objection.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The man was right that the dates were his. רב כהנא credits רבי יאשיה's lasting Torah influence for the man's knowledge.

steps.title: Poor non-Jews may take the poor's gifts from the field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: we do not stop poor non-Jews from taking לקט, שכחה and פאה, because of דרכי שלום.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not stop poor non-Jews from taking gleanings, forgotten sheaves, or the corner of the field, because of the ways of peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה it has been explaining. This line is about poor non-Jews taking the gifts left in the field for the poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, לקט, שכחה and פאה are left for poor Jews. Still, the חכמים said not to chase poor non-Jews away from them. The reason is to keep good relations with them.

keyTerms.meaning: protest against, stop someone
stalks that fall while harvesting, left for the poor
sheaves forgotten in the field, left for the poor
the corner of the field left unharvested for the poor
the ways of peace, keeping good relations

phrases.english: One does not protest against poor gentiles
who take gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field,
because of the ways of peace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story of רב כהנא, the גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Poor non-Jews are not stopped from taking לקט, שכחה and פאה, because of דרכי שלום.

steps.title: Supporting, visiting and burying non-Jews together with Jews
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that we support poor non-Jews, visit their sick and bury their dead together with Jews, because of דרכי שלום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: We support poor non-Jews along with poor Jews. We visit sick non-Jews along with sick Jews. We bury dead non-Jews along with dead Jews. All this is because of the ways of peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with more examples of the same idea. Kindness to non-Jews is done for the sake of peace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה spoke only about gifts from the field. The ברייתא widens this to צדקה, visiting the sick and burial. The word 'together with' shows that these acts are done side by side with the same acts for Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: the Rabbis taught (opens a ברייתא)
we support, provide for
we visit (the sick)
we bury

steps.whatToRemember: Many acts of kindness toward non-Jews (gifts from the field, צדקה, visiting the sick, burial) are done because of דרכי שלום.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: מְפַרְנְסִים עֲנִיֵּי גוֹיִם עִם עֲנִיֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: We support poor gentiles along with poor Jews,

phrases.aramaic: וּמְבַקְּרִין חוֹלֵי גוֹיִם עִם חוֹלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: and we visit sick gentiles along with sick Jews,

phrases.aramaic: וְקוֹבְרִין מֵתֵי גוֹיִם עִם מֵתֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: and we bury dead gentiles along with dead Jews,
because of the ways of peace.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מְפַרְנְסִים עֲנִיֵּי גוֹיִם עִם עֲנִיֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that widens the משנה's idea of דרכי שלום toward non-Jews.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Poor non-Jews are supported, their sick visited and their dead buried along with Jews, because of דרכי שלום.

steps.title: Lending tools to a woman suspected about שביעית
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a woman may lend kitchen tools to a friend suspected about שביעית, but may not sift or grind with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A woman may lend her friend who is suspected about שביעית a winnow, a sieve, a mill and an oven. But she may not sort or grind together with her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches how far one woman may help another woman who may be eating שביעית produce she should not eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lending a tool is allowed, since the friend might use it in a permitted way. Working together with her on the forbidden food is direct help with a sin, so that is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: short for מתניתין, 'our משנה'
the seventh (שמיטה) year and the laws of its produce
suspected (of not keeping a law)
a winnow or fine sifter
a sieve

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up lending and helping. Lending the tools is allowed. Doing the work together with her is not.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A woman may lend to her friend
who is suspected regarding the Sabbatical Year –
a winnow, a sieve, a mill, and an oven.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא תָּבוֹר וְלֹא תִּטְחַן עִמָּהּ.
phrases.english: But she may not sort or grind together with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַשְׁאֶלֶת אִשָּׁה לַחֲבֶירְתָּהּ הַחֲשׁוּדָה עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה about the limits of helping someone who may sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lending tools to a woman suspected about שביעית is allowed. Doing the work with her is forbidden.

steps.title: Helping an עם הארץ's wife until the water is added
steps.stepSummary: The wife of a חבר may lend tools to the wife of an עם הארץ and even work with her, but not after water is added to the flour. All these allowances are because of דרכי שלום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wife of a חבר may lend the wife of an עם הארץ a winnow and a sieve. She may even sort, grind and sift with her. But once the other woman pours in the water, she may not touch anything with her, because we do not help people who do a sin. All these allowances were said only because of the ways of peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case: the wife of a careful person helping the wife of someone who is not careful about טהרה. Here she may help more, but only up to the point of adding water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before water is added, she may work side by side with the עם הארץ's wife. Once the water goes in, helping counts as helping a sin, so it is forbidden. The גמרא in steps 17-18 explains why water is the turning point, and the closing line says all the earlier allowances were given for the sake of peace.

keyTerms.meaning: a person careful about טהרה and מעשרות
a person not careful about these laws
sifts (flour)
strengthening the hands of sinners, helping them sin

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a clear dividing line. Helping before a sin starts may be allowed for peace. Direct help during the sin is not.

phrases.aramaic: אֵשֶׁת חָבֵר מַשְׁאֶלֶת לְאֵשֶׁת עַם הָאָרֶץ –
phrases.english: The wife of a ḥaver may lend the wife of an am ha'aretz –
a winnow and a sieve;
and she may sort, grind, and sift with her;
but once she pours in the water –
she may not touch anything with her,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מַחְזִיקִין יְדֵי עוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵירָה.
phrases.english: because one may not strengthen the hands of those who sin.

phrases.aramaic: וְכוּלָּן לֹא אָמְרוּ, אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי דַּרְכֵי שָׁלוֹם.
phrases.english: And all of these they said only because of the ways of peace.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵשֶׁת חָבֵר מַשְׁאֶלֶת לְאֵשֶׁת עַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the same משנה, which allows more help, up to the point where a sin begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Working with the עם הארץ's wife is allowed until water is added. After that it is forbidden, since one may not help sinners. These allowances exist because of דרכי שלום.

steps.title: Helping non-Jews during שביעית and greeting them
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends: one may help non-Jews working the land in שביעית, but not Jews, and one may greet non-Jews, because of דרכי שלום.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may help non-Jews during שביעית, but not Jews. And one may greet them, because of the ways of peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with two more rules about non-Jews. Both are allowed for the sake of peace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-Jew is not commanded to keep שביעית, so helping him is not helping a sin. A Jew who works the land in שביעית is sinning, so helping him is forbidden. Greeting non-Jews is also allowed for peace.

keyTerms.meaning: the hands of Jews (helping Jews)
we greet them, ask about their wellbeing

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of thumb: kindness for דרכי שלום is encouraged, but never direct help to a Jew who is doing a sin.

phrases.english: And one may help gentiles during the Sabbatical Year –
phrases.notes: He means helping them while they work the land.

phrases.english: but not Jews;
and one may greet them,
because of the ways of peace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the משנה by applying the same rule (no helping sinners, but keeping peace) to non-Jews.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may help non-Jews working in שביעית but not Jews, and one may greet non-Jews, because of דרכי שלום.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why helping a friend suspected about שביעית is forbidden, while helping the wife of an עם הארץ is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is different about the first case, and what is different about the second case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking why the משנה treats two similar cases differently. This question sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, a woman may lend tools to a friend suspected about שביעית, but she may not sift or grind with her. In the סיפא, the wife of a חבר may even sift and grind with the wife of an עם הארץ. Both women may be preparing forbidden food, so why is one allowed and the other not?

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה
What is different? Why the change?
The first part of the משנה
The later part of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is different in the first clause,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the friend suspected about שביעית: you may not sift or grind with her.

phrases.english: and what is different in the latter clause?
phrases.notes: The latter clause is the wife of a חבר, who may even work together with the wife of an עם הארץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא, וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה quoted in steps 11-12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the משנה is strict in one case and lenient in the other.

steps.title: אביי: most עמי הארץ separate מעשרות
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the wife of an עם הארץ is probably preparing permitted food, because most עמי הארץ do separate מעשרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Most עמי הארץ do separate מעשרות.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first answer to the question. Helping the wife of an עם הארץ is allowed because her food is probably fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The friend suspected about שביעית is presumed to be preparing forbidden food, so helping her is forbidden. The עם הארץ, however, most likely separated מעשרות, so his wife is probably preparing permitted food. Because of דרכי שלום, we do not worry about the minority who don't separate מעשרות.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the first answer
People who are not careful about certain הלכות
They separate מעשרות (tithes)
Most, the majority

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Most amei ha'aretz tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רוֹב עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מְעַשְּׂרִין הֵן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is the רוב: most עמי הארץ separate מעשרות, so their food is presumed permitted.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה means רבי מאיר's עם הארץ and rabbinic purity
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the עם הארץ in the משנה is רבי מאיר's kind, who does separate מעשרות but does not eat his ordinary food in purity. That purity is only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Here we are dealing with an עם הארץ as רבי מאיר defines him, and with purity rules that are דרבנן. As a ברייתא teaches: Who is an עם הארץ? Anyone who does not eat his חולין in purity. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: Anyone who does not separate מעשרות from his produce.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. He says the משנה is not worried about מעשרות at all, only about purity of ordinary food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, an עם הארץ is someone who separates מעשרות but is not careful to eat his חולין in purity. Keeping חולין pure is only a rabbinic matter, so the חכמים allowed working with his wife because of דרכי שלום. The friend suspected about שביעית is suspected of a real prohibition, so that case stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the second answer
Laws of impurity and purity
A rule made by the חכמים, not from the Torah
Ordinary food that is not holy
As a ברייתא teaches

steps.confusionAlert: The term עם הארץ means different things to different תנאים. For רבי מאיר it means someone careless about purity. For the חכמים it means someone who does not separate מעשרות.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Here it is about the am ha'aretz of Rabbi Meir,
and about impurity and purity that are rabbinic –
as it is taught: Who is an am ha'aretz?
Anyone who does not eat his non-sacred food in purity,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Rabbis say:
Anyone who does not tithe his produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הָכָא בְּעַם הָאָרֶץ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 14, different from אביי's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עם הארץ in the משנה is רבי מאיר's type, so the only concern is rabbinic purity of חולין, which is set aside for דרכי שלום.

steps.title: The 'once she adds water' line seems to show the first part is not about purity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא. Since the משנה makes adding water the turning point for purity, the earlier part must be about something else, like מעשרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the later clause teaches, 'Once she adds the water, she may not touch anything with her,' this shows that in the first clause we are not dealing with impurity and purity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's answer using the משנה's own wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding water is what makes food able to become impure. If the משנה only forbids helping after water is added, then before that point purity cannot be the issue. So the permission to sift and grind seems to be about מעשרות, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it teaches
Once she adds the water
This shows / we can infer
We are dealing with

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches:

phrases.aramaic: מִשֶּׁתָּטִיל אֶת הַמַּיִם לֹא תִּגַּע עִמָּהּ;
phrases.english: once she pours the water she may not touch anything with her;
phrases.notes: Water makes flour able to become impure.

phrases.english: it follows that in the first clause,
phrases.notes: Here 'the first clause' means the sifting and grinding, before water is added.

phrases.english: we are not dealing with impurity and purity!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the משנה is talking about purity.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats adding water as the point where purity begins to matter, so the earlier permission cannot be about purity.

steps.title: Both parts are about purity: first חולין, then חלה
steps.stepSummary: Both parts of the משנה are about purity. Before water is added, the concern is only טומאת חולין, which is rabbinic. After water, the dough must have חלה taken from it, and making חלה impure is forbidden by the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both the first clause and the latter clause are about impurity and purity. The first clause is about the impurity of חולין, and the latter clause is about the impurity of חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. Both parts deal with purity, but they deal with two different levels of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While she sifts and grinds, the most that could happen is that ordinary food becomes impure. That is only rabbinic, so it is set aside for דרכי שלום. Once water is added, the dough becomes obligated in חלה, and causing חלה to become impure is a Torah prohibition, so helping is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity of ordinary food, a rabbinic concern
Impurity of the dough portion given to a כהן, a Torah concern
The piece of dough separated and given to a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: אביי says the עם הארץ is allowed because most of them separate מעשרות. רבא says it is because the issue is only rabbinic purity of חולין. The גמרא defends רבא: helping becomes forbidden once water is added, because then the concern is טומאת חלה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that דרכי שלום can set aside a rabbinic concern, but not a Torah prohibition.

phrases.english: The first clause and the latter clause are both about impurity and purity;
and the first clause – about impurity of non-sacred food,
and the latter clause – about impurity of challah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 and upholds רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two parts into two different levels of purity.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since adding water is the turning point, the part before water must not be about purity.
steps.terutzMaskana: Before water the concern is rabbinic טומאת חולין, which is allowed for דרכי שלום. After water the concern is Torah-level טומאת חלה, which is forbidden.

steps.title: Setting up a contradiction from another source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא signals that it is about to quote a source that seems to clash with what was just explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא raises a contradiction:
steps.whatsHappening: This one word is a setup line. The גמרא is telling us that it is about to quote another source that seems to contradict the ruling it just finished explaining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the גמרא concluded that helping an עם הארץ's wife is allowed, since before water is added the only purity concern is rabbinic. 'וּרְמִינְהוּ' warns that a ברייתא coming next seems to rule differently. The real argument starts in the next step, when that source is quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they set them against each other': the standard signal that the גמרא is about to show two sources that seem to contradict
Literally 'to throw'. Here it means to set one source against another
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה itself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't expect an argument in this step. 'וּרְמִינְהוּ' only announces the contradiction. The conflicting source comes right after it.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תירוץ in step 18 settled how the משנה works, the גמרא now opens a new challenge by bringing an outside source that seems to conflict.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that one may help the wife of an עם הארץ prepare food, as explained in steps 15 to 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction between sources (סתירה). Another ברייתא, quoted next, seems to rule differently, so the two sources need to be reconciled.
